title: How and when to apply worm castings
subtitle: Application rates, dilution for liquid feed, and which crops benefit most
excerpt: Worm castings are a concentrated soil amendment: small quantities have outsized effects compared with ordinary compost. The typical application rate is 10 to 20% by volume mixed into growing medium, or 1 to 2 litres per m² as a surface dressing. Diluted casting liquid is an effective liquid feed at 1:10 with water.
sourceNotes: Clive Edwards and Norman Arancon (Ohio State University) research on vermicompost application rates, published in peer-reviewed form 2004 to 2011. RHS guidance on worm compost application. WRAP guidance on organic matter application rates in gardens.

glossaryTerms.definition: The end product of composting with earthworms. Worm castings are rich in available nutrients, plant growth hormones, and beneficial microbes.

content.text: when mixed with other partially broken-down material) are more concentrated than ordinary compost. Seedling trials show improved germination and early root mass at low rates. At high rates, growth can slow in some species.
Seed-starting mix: 10 to 20% castings by volume mixed into a neutral seed compost. Higher proportions can inhibit germination in slow-germinating seeds.
Potting mix for established plants: 20 to 30% castings by volume mixed into multi-purpose compost.
Surface dressing on beds: 1 to 2 litres per m². Work lightly into the surface or leave as a mulch for worms to incorporate.
Planting hole for transplants: one handful (approximately 200 ml) in the base of each planting hole, mixed with the backfill soil.

Casting liquid (the diluted leachate from a wormery collecting tray) should be used at 1 part liquid to 10 parts water. It is ready to use when poured fresh; do not store liquid leachate for more than 24 hours as it becomes anaerobic and can harm seedlings.

Aerated worm tea (made by bubbling air through a casting suspension for 24 hours) maintains a higher beneficial microbial count. Use a small aquarium pump and 1 litre of castings in 10 litres of dechlorinated water. Apply within 4 hours of the aeration finishing.
Tomatoes, peppers, and aubergines: add castings to the potting mix for best results.
Seedlings of all types: a low-rate casting mix speeds root development. It avoids the damping-off risk from high-nitrogen feeds.
Houseplants: a handful of castings worked into the top 50 mm of potting compost twice a year provides slow-release nutrition.

rows.symptom: Seedlings growing in a high-casting mix are yellow and stunted
rows.cause: Casting concentration above 25% by volume can inhibit germination or cause salt stress in fine-rooted seedlings
rows.fix: Reduce casting proportion to 10% and dilute the mix with a neutral compost. Water the tray thoroughly to flush excess salts.

rows.symptom: Worm leachate smells foul rather than earthy
rows.cause: Leachate has become anaerobic in the collection tray
rows.fix: Empty and clean the tray. Use leachate within 24 hours of collection. If the wormery itself smells bad, the bin is overloaded or too wet.
